who: Book of Rites (Liji), Qu Li I, tr. James Legge, 1885
quote: I have heard ... of (scholars) coming to learn; I have not heard of (the master) going to teach.
meaning: Go to the teacher. The teacher will not come to you.

who: Han Yu · On the Teacher, about 802, tr. Shih Shun Liu, 1977
quote: In ancient times scholars always had teachers... Since man is not born with knowledge, who can be without doubt? But doubt will never be resolved without a teacher.
meaning: No one is born knowing. Long ago, every learner found a teacher to clear their doubts.

who: Bhagavad Gita 4.34 · tr. K. T. Telang, 1882
quote: ...you should learn by salutation, question, and service. The men of knowledge who perceive the truth will teach knowledge to you.
meaning: Bow, ask good questions, and help. Then the people who know will teach you.

who: Xuanzang, monk, 7th century · Huili, The Life of Hiuen-Tsiang, tr. Samuel Beal, 1888
quote: The monk Xuanzang found that China's teachers and books disagreed, so he went to India. At Nalanda he told the teacher Silabhadra: ‘I am come from the country of China, desiring to learn from your instruction...’
meaning: His teachers did not agree, so he travelled all the way to India to find the right one.

who: Zeno of Citium · Diogenes Laertius, Lives VII.2-4, tr. R. D. Hicks, 1925
quote: Zeno, then thirty, read about Socrates in an Athens bookshop and asked where such men could be found. Crates passed by, and the bookseller said: ‘Follow yonder man.’ Zeno studied with teachers for twenty years.
meaning: He asked where a real teacher was. One walked by, and he followed.

who: J. S. Bach · Obituary, 1754; his words to the Arnstadt council, 1706, in Spitta, tr. 1884
quote: In 1705 the organist J. S. Bach, 20, got four weeks off and walked hundreds of kilometres to Lübeck to hear Buxtehude. He stayed away four months, ‘to learn thoroughly one or two things connected with his art.’
meaning: If the best teacher is far away, go to him, even on foot.

who: Michael Faraday · his notes, in Bence Jones, The Life and Letters of Faraday, 1870
quote: In 1812 Michael Faraday, 21, a bookbinder, longed for science. ‘I wrote to Sir Humphry Davy, sending, as a proof of my earnestness, the notes I had taken of his last four lectures.’ By 1813 he was Davy's assistant.
meaning: Do not wait to be picked. Show your hard work and ask to learn.

quote: Rather than spend three years studying hard, better to spend three years choosing a teacher.
meaning: The right teacher is worth more than years of studying alone.

quote: A student who has a teacher.
meaning: When someone is really good, Thai people say: they had a good teacher.

who: K. Pattabhi Jois · as told by Eddie Stern, foreword to Yoga Mala, 2010
quote: In 1927, twelve-year-old Pattabhi Jois watched T. Krishnamacharya's demonstration in Hassan. The next day he rose early, went to the yogi's house and asked to be taught. He was told to come back the next day.
meaning: A 12-year-old asked to learn the very next day. He grew up to teach the Ashtanga we practise.
